display.purpose: Brand name S.M BROWS only. One per page. Expressed in serif (Dancing Script for Latin, Noto Serif Hebrew for Hebrew).

headline.purpose: Section headings. Always serif. Never more than one per section.

title.purpose: Card headings, service names, blog titles. Serif.

body.purpose: All prose, descriptions, and paragraph text. Rubik. Max 65ch line length. Color: Rose Bark Medium (#6B4545).

label.purpose: Eyebrow tags above headings, category chips, section labels. Rubik semibold. Uppercase, tracked at 0.2em. Gold Text (#725417) or Rose Text (#96534A) based on context.

shadows.name: soft
shadows.purpose: Cards and contained surfaces at rest. Warm, barely-there lift.

shadows.name: soft-lg
shadows.purpose: Card hover state and hero image container. Earned lift on interaction.

shadows.name: rose-glow
shadows.purpose: Optional warm rose halo for featured accent elements.

shadows.name: gold-glow
shadows.purpose: Optional warm gold halo for premium or featured surfaces.

shadows.name: menu
shadows.purpose: Dropdown menus and modal overlays. Deepest ambient shadow in the system.

motion.name: ease-spring
motion.purpose: Primary easing for all entrance and interaction transitions. Spring-like ease-out — fast start, graceful landing.

motion.name: rise
motion.purpose: Above-fold hero text entrance. Transform-only (no opacity) so LCP content is visible on first paint.

motion.name: fade-up
motion.purpose: Section content entrance below the fold. Staggered per child with 80ms delay increments.

motion.name: reveal
motion.purpose: Scroll-triggered reveal for section children. y: 22px → 0, opacity 0 → 1. Respects prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: float
motion.purpose: Idle decorative float on ambient elements. y: 0 → -8px → 0.

motion.name: nav-transition
motion.purpose: Navigation transparency → frosted transition on scroll.

components.name: Loading, Disabled, Success, and Error States
components.description: Explicit state definitions required in every redesign. No cold greys or clinical greens/reds — all states use the warm palette. Loading: rose spinner. Disabled: warm palette at 0.45 opacity. Success: gold-accented, calm and warm. Error: Rose Text (#96534A), clear resolution path.

narrative.overview:
S.M BROWS is a single-practitioner studio, and the design system carries that fact structurally. Every surface is warm without being soft, precise without being clinical. There is no corporate polish here — this is a skilled artisan's space, and the interface is its interior: hand-chosen materials, warm light, nothing extraneous. The brand's warmth is not decorative tone applied over a neutral template; it comes from the palette, the corner language, the typefaces, and the weight of every element working together.

The system lives at a quiet intersection of intimacy and professionalism. Sections breathe with generous vertical rhythm. Cards feel weighted and considered. The typography pairs an expressive Hebrew/Latin serif with a clean, highly legible sans-serif, creating a pairing that is simultaneously personal and credible. The result is a design that does not look like a beauty template — it looks like Shoval.

Color is warm throughout, with no cold neutrals. Depth is conveyed through tonal layering — warm ivory body → linen → white — rather than dramatic shadows. The UI is RTL (Hebrew-first), and the spatial logic flows from right to left.
keyCharacteristics: Warm ivory body with linen and rose-tinted layering; no cold greys or blues
RTL (Hebrew) spatial logic throughout all surfaces
Pillow-edged cards (24–32px radius) and pill-shaped primary CTAs; secondary surfaces use 12–16px corners
Serif headings (Dancing Script / Noto Serif Hebrew) over Rubik body; expressive but readable
Tonal depth rather than structural shadows; shadows are warm and appear primarily on hover
Motion is spring-like and purposeful: cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), 0.55–0.7s, respects prefers-reduced-motion
Gold focus rings; accessible rose/gold color pairs confirmed to WCAG AA

locked: Brand identity: name 'S.M BROWS', tagline 'IT'S ALL ABOUT YOUR EYEBROWS', and Shoval's personal voice throughout
Core color palette: Warm Ivory, Dusty Petal Rose, Soft Champagne Gold, Deep Espresso, and all documented supporting tokens
Font families: Dancing Script + Noto Serif Hebrew (heading stack) and Rubik (body/label stack) — sizes, weights, and hierarchy are open
Logo: /public/logo.png — exact asset, never replaced or modified

Authentic client media: all before/after photos, testimonial screenshots, and treatment videos in /public are real — may be reframed, repositioned, or presented in new layouts; content and authenticity may not be altered
Factual content: pricing, service names, booking rules, contact details, location, hours, legal text, and the prohibition on displaying a course price
Hebrew-first RTL: the site is in Hebrew, reads right to left, and is designed for Israeli mobile users
open: Section layouts and overall visual hierarchy
Typography scale and weights (font families are locked)
Border and radius usage within the warm visual language
Button shapes and interactive surface design
Media containers and their aspect ratios
Booking UI presentation and step flow
redesignFreedom.designDirection: The existing UI is correct in identity but conservative in execution. The redesign should amplify what is already true — precision, warmth, personal craft — and eliminate the generic or safe. A premium boutique studio should feel like one in every detail, from the section rhythm to the way a before/after image is framed to the moment a button responds to a touch.

mediaPrinciples: Never stretch or distort media. object-fit: cover or object-fit: contain, never fill without explicit intent.

Use deliberate aspect ratios (4/3, 3/4, 1/1, 16/9). Container height must be determined by a meaningful aspect ratio or a content-aware decision — not by an arbitrary fixed pixel value inherited from a utility class.
object-position must be chosen per image, not defaulted. Faces, brows, and treatment results are always the subject; the framing decision is a design decision made for each image.
Faces and brows must never be unintentionally cropped. The eyebrows are the product — a portrait that cuts off brows or foreheads is a failed presentation.
Media must remain sharp and properly framed across breakpoints. Framing decisions made at desktop must be verified at mobile; the subject must remain correctly framed at all sizes.

A source image may be visually reframed or repositioned. Cropping to better frame the subject, adjusting object-position, or choosing a tighter aspect ratio are valid design decisions that do not alter authenticity.
Avoid tiny letterboxed images. An image compressed into an oversized container surrounded by bands of background color is worse than no image.

Video presentation must feel intentional and premium: deliberate poster frames, considered aspect ratios, and presentation contexts that signal craft — not raw embedded media elements dropped into a layout.
narrative.baselineDisclaimer: All component entries marked with 'baseline: true' document the current implementation as a starting point for redesign — not a final design to preserve. Card composition, section layout, button shape, image treatment, and every other visual decision are open to significant evolution. What cannot change is the brand identity, palette, font families, and authentic content documented in redesignFreedom.

rules.name: The Warm-Only Rule
rules.body: No cold greys, blues, or neutral tones are introduced anywhere in the system. Every neutral carries red or yellow warmth. When in doubt, test: the new color's undertone must be warm.

rules.name: The Two-Accent Rule
rules.body: Rose and Gold are the only accents. Rose governs emotion, warmth, and interactive hover states. Gold governs prestige, focus, and precision. They do not overlap in function.

rules.name: The Script-Serif Rule
rules.body: All headings and price displays use the serif stack. Rubik is body only. A heading set in Rubik is incorrect regardless of weight.

rules.name: The Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Category labels above headings are always uppercase, tracked at 0.2em, and set in Rubik semibold at 12–14px. They orient the reader; they are never bold enough to compete with the headline.

rules.name: The Flat-at-Rest Rule
rules.body: Cards and interactive surfaces carry shadow-soft at rest — present but not assertive. The shadow grows on hover (shadow-soft-lg + -translate-y-1). Depth is earned through interaction, not baked in at full intensity from the start.

rules.name: The Warm Shadow Rule
rules.body: All box shadows are derived from Deep Espresso (#2C1810), not neutral black. A neutral black shadow on a warm-toned surface reads as dirty; the warm base shadow disappears into the palette.

rules.name: The Radius Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Corners loosen with surface dominance. Hero image: 32px. Cards: 24px. Menus: 16px. Inputs: 12px. Icon buttons: 8px. Never assign a tighter radius to a more dominant element.

dos: Do use the serif stack (Dancing Script + Noto Serif Hebrew) for every heading level — display, headline, title. Rubik is body only.
Do set all layout from RTL (dir="rtl"). Use logical properties (ps, pe, ms, me) instead of pl/pr/ml/mr in new code.
Do use warm-toned shadows derived from rgba(44, 24, 16, ...) for all depth effects. Never use rgba(0, 0, 0, ...).
Do use gold (#C9A96E) for all focus rings (outline: 2px solid #C9A96E; outline-offset: 3px).
Do source new before/after images and testimonials only from real client work. Authenticity is core to the brand.
Do choose deliberate aspect ratios for every image and video container. A pixel height pulled from a utility class is not a framing decision.
Do set object-position deliberately for every portrait or treatment image. The brows must always be visible.
Do verify media framing at mobile sizes, not just desktop. The subject must remain correctly framed after the container reflows.
Do treat video poster frames as editorial choices — the frame that best represents the content and result.
donts: Don't introduce any cold grey, blue, or neutral tone. Every surface must carry warm undertone.
Don't display or invent a price for the course — it is discussed privately via WhatsApp and must remain undisclosed in the UI.
Don't fabricate or write testimonials, review text, or before/after descriptions. Only real WhatsApp screenshots from /public may be used.
Don't apply shadows in neutral black. All shadow colors must be warm (espresso-based or rose-based).
Don't set headings in Rubik. The serif stack is non-negotiable for brand voice.
Don't introduce a second accent color. Rose and Gold are the entire accent vocabulary.
Don't stretch, distort, or letterbox media. An image compressed into an oversized container is worse than no image.
Don't crop a portrait at the forehead or mid-brow. The eyebrows are the product — they must always be visible and properly framed.
Don't treat the existing component shapes, card layouts, section structures, or spacing rhythm as final. This documentation records where the design is, not where it must stay.
